historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved a $2.6 million master plan for Buena Vista Park, drawn up through community meetings, centered on replanting the park's very old trees, erosion control and signs, with later renovation of the tennis courts; a $163,972 automatic irrigation system had been let to Munkdale Bros. in February.
Named Buena Vista Park by the state act of April 4, 1870 that created Golden Gate Park, and placed with it under the new Board of Park Commissioners.
A carriage drive was built up to the summit, for the view over the ocean, the bay and the country around.
Laid out to plans drawn after an 1896 survey: macadam paths around the hill and rustic steps up from Haight Street.
